sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the June 2025 Class Health Care Support Assistant College Final Exam, Cicely McDonnell College of Health Sciences (19 November 2025), Multiple Choice Questions Q41 to Q60. Q57 has two True/False statements, (a) and (b), each listed as its own question.

questions.text: Patient K has fractures of the pelvis. The ideal type of bath a health care assistant should offer is:
questions.explanation: Complete bed bath (D) is correct because a patient with a fractured pelvis must stay on bed rest and avoid movement, weight bearing and unnecessary turning, so the HCA does the whole bath for the patient in bed, moving the patient as little as possible and with the nurse's guidance on safe positioning (for example log-rolling). A tub bath (A) and a shower bath (B) need the patient to get out of bed and bear weight, which could displace the fracture. An assisted bed bath (C) expects the patient to wash the parts they can reach, which involves movement and effort that is unsafe here.

questions.text: Why should health care assistant promote patient independence during bed bath?

options.A: To reduce the work an HCA
options.B: To ensure patient perform daily exercises
options.C: To assist the patient anticipate their hygienic needs

questions.explanation: To assist the patient anticipate their hygienic needs (C) is the best answer because encouraging patients to do what they can for themselves (washing their face, hands and front of the body) keeps them involved in their own care, so they learn to recognise and plan for their hygiene needs, and this builds self-esteem and dignity and speeds recovery. Reducing the HCA's work (A) is never the reason. Exercise (B) may be a small side benefit but is not the purpose of independence in bathing. Privacy (D) is promoted by drawing curtains and exposing only the part being washed, which is a separate principle from independence. If your lecture notes give a different key, follow your notes.

questions.text: A nurse and an HCA are admitting a patient. A role of an HCA will include:

options.B: Performing physical examination on the patient
options.D: Administration of prescribed intravenous pain reliever medication

questions.explanation: Preparing the patient's room appropriately (A) is correct because the HCA's role during admission is to get the bed and room ready (clean, made-up bed, working equipment, call bell, locker, privacy screens), welcome and orient the patient and family, help with changing and belongings, and take and record vital signs and weight when instructed. Performing a physical examination (B) and taking the history (C) are done by the nurse or clinician. Administering IV medication (D) is outside the HCA's scope of practice.

questions.text: As the HCA triage the patient, they understand that triage:

options.A: Ensures that very sick patient receive medical attention immediately
options.B: Allows the patient to be seen at the basis of first come first serve
options.C: Allows the patient to follow the queue regardless of their condition
options.D: Can be performed by any person as long as the patient gets the attention

questions.explanation: Ensures that very sick patients receive medical attention immediately (A) is correct because triage is the process of sorting patients by the urgency of their condition so that the most critically ill are seen first (emergency, priority, queue), rather than by arrival time. First come first served (B) and following the queue regardless of condition (C) would delay care for life-threatening cases. Triage must be done by trained, authorised health workers, so (D) is wrong; the HCA supports by measuring vital signs and reporting danger signs immediately.

questions.text: Which is the best position to nurse a patient immediately postoperatively?
questions.explanation: Sim's (D) is correct because the semi-prone or recovery position (Sim's position) keeps the airway open, lets saliva, mucus or vomit drain from the mouth and prevents the tongue falling back, which protects an unconscious or drowsy post-operative patient from airway obstruction and aspiration until they regain consciousness. Prone (A) restricts chest movement and breathing. Supine (B) is not safe for an unconscious patient because of aspiration and tongue fall-back, although it is used after some procedures such as spinal anaesthesia on the nurse's instructions. Trendelenburg (C) (head down) increases pressure on the diaphragm and risks aspiration.

questions.text: What device should an HCA set up when the doctor orders the patient to be commenced on oxygen at 2 Litres/minute?
questions.explanation: Nasal prongs (A) are correct because they are used for low-flow oxygen of about 1 to 4 litres per minute and deliver a low concentration of oxygen (about 24 to 36%), and are comfortable and allow the patient to eat and talk. A simple face mask (B) needs at least 5 to 6 L/min to flush out exhaled carbon dioxide. A non-rebreather mask (C) delivers high-flow oxygen of 10 to 15 L/min for critically ill patients. Breathing tubes (D) means endotracheal tubes or mechanical ventilation, which are not used for a 2 L/min order.

questions.text: The normal resting pulse rate for an adult is between:
questions.explanation: 60-100 beats/min (B) is correct because this is the accepted normal resting pulse range for a healthy adult. A rate below 60 is bradycardia (although well-trained athletes may normally have a lower rate), and a rate above 100 is tachycardia, which may be due to fever, pain, anxiety, bleeding, shock or heart problems. The HCA counts the pulse for a full minute, notes the rate, rhythm and strength, and reports abnormal findings to the nurse. Options A, C and D lie outside the normal range.

questions.text: The instrument used to measure blood pressure is called:
questions.explanation: Sphygmomanometer (B) is correct because it is the instrument made of a cuff, a bulb and a pressure gauge (mercury, aneroid or digital) that measures blood pressure in mmHg. A spirometer (A) measures lung volumes, a stethoscope (C) is used to listen to body sounds, including the Korotkoff sounds when taking manual blood pressure, but it does not measure pressure, and a thermometer (D) measures body temperature.

questions.text: The first step in collecting a specimen is:

options.B: Explaining the procedure to the patient
options.D: Sending the specimen to the lab

questions.explanation: Explaining the procedure to the patient (B) is correct because the patient must understand what is being done and why, and must give consent and cooperate (for example, a clean mid-stream urine or early-morning sputum), which makes a good-quality specimen more likely and respects their rights. After this the HCA washes hands, wears gloves, collects the specimen in the correct container, labels it with the patient's details and sends it promptly to the lab with the request form. Labeling (A), wearing gloves (C) and sending to the lab (D) come after the explanation, with sending to the lab being the last step.

questions.text: The role of HCA in wound care is to:

options.B: Infection control and change of antiseptic
options.C: Identify antiseptic for use and documentation

questions.explanation: Monitoring wound healing and cleaning (D) is correct because the HCA, under the nurse's supervision, assists with cleaning and dressing wounds as directed, keeps the area clean and dry, uses aseptic technique, observes for signs of delay or infection (redness, swelling, heat, pain, pus, odour, fever) and reports to the nurse. Full wound assessment (A) and choosing or changing antiseptics (B, C) are clinical decisions made by the nurse or clinician. Note that (A), (B) and (C) include tasks that are outside the HCA's scope.

questions.text: What are the factors affecting wound healing?
questions.explanation: Infection and nutrition (C) is correct because both are well-established factors in wound healing: infection delays healing by prolonging inflammation and destroying tissue, and poor nutrition (lack of protein, vitamin C, zinc and calories) slows tissue repair. Other factors include age, blood supply and oxygenation, diabetes, smoking, medications such as steroids, and moisture and pressure on the wound. In the other options, height (A) and gender (B, D) do not directly influence healing, so each option includes at least one factor that does not belong.

questions.text: A bed appliance that is used to prevent external rotation of the leg is:
questions.explanation: Trochanter roll (D) is correct because it is a rolled towel or blanket (or a commercial roll) placed along the outer side of the thigh, from the hip to the knee, to prevent the hip and leg from rolling outwards (external rotation), which helps keep the leg in correct alignment and prevents contractures and pressure on the ankle. A wedge pillow (A) is used to hold a patient in a side-lying position or to elevate the body, a fracture board (B) is placed under the mattress to provide a firm base, and sandbags (C) can also support limbs but the trochanter roll is the specific device for preventing external rotation.

questions.text: A type of bed made when the patient cannot get out of the bed is:
questions.explanation: Occupied bed (B) is correct because it is made while the patient is lying in it, for patients who are unable to get out of bed because of illness, injury or surgery. The HCA works from one side to the other, turning the patient and keeping the patient covered, warm and safe. A post-operative bed (A) is prepared for a patient returning from theatre. An empty or unoccupied bed (C, D) is made when the patient is out of bed, for example for a patient who is up in the chair or going to the toilet.

questions.text: The patient requests the health care assistant to allow her time to rest before taking lunch. The health care assistant complies to this request in line with the ethical principle of:
questions.explanation: Autonomy (A) is correct because autonomy is the patient's right to make decisions about their own care and to be respected in these decisions; allowing the patient to choose when to eat is respecting this. Veracity (B) is truthfulness. Fidelity (C) is keeping promises and being faithful to commitments. Confidentiality (D) is protecting the patient's private information.

questions.text: What must be contained in an employment contract for a HCA?
questions.explanation: Position hired for (C) is correct because an employment contract must set out the essential terms of the job: the employer and employee, the job title or position, duties, pay, working hours, place of work, start date and duration. The process of seeking leave (A) is normally in the staff policy or regulations. Appreciation of services (B) and names of coworkers (D) are not required contract terms.

questions.text: A healthcare assistant is assigned to care of a famous person on homecare. The health care assistant posts her photo with the background identifying the patient in their home on her WhatsApp status. The assistant is liable for:
questions.explanation: Invasion of privacy (D) is correct because posting a photo that identifies the patient and shows them in their home discloses their private information and breaches the confidentiality and dignity owed to patients, and can lead to legal action and professional discipline. Battery (A) is unlawful physical contact and assault (B) is a threat of unlawful force. Slander (C) is a spoken false statement that damages someone's reputation, which is not what happened here.

questions.text: True or False: An ethical dilemma includes the regulations a profession must adhere to.
questions.explanation: FALSE. An ethical dilemma is a situation in which a person must choose between two or more actions that each conflict with ethical principles or values, so that every option has a cost (for example, a patient asks the HCA to keep a secret that may affect their safety). The regulations a profession must adhere to are laws, standards and rules of practice, not an ethical dilemma.

questions.text: True or False: Code of conduct guides the behavior and ethics of a profession.
questions.explanation: TRUE. A code of conduct is a written set of rules and standards that describes the expected behaviour, values and ethical responsibilities of members of a profession, such as respect, honesty, confidentiality, accountability and acting in the patient's best interest. It guides health workers in their daily practice and is used to hold them accountable.

questions.text: Which of the following cranial nerves is responsible for smell?
questions.explanation: Olfactory (B) is correct because the olfactory nerve (cranial nerve I) carries the sense of smell from the nose to the brain. The optic nerve (A, cranial nerve II) is for vision, the vestibulocochlear nerve (C, cranial nerve VIII) is for hearing and balance, and the glossopharyngeal nerve (D, cranial nerve IX) supplies taste on the back of the tongue and swallowing.

questions.text: A part of the ear that collects and concentrates sound waves and directs them along the auditory canal is:
questions.explanation: Auricle (A) is correct because the auricle (pinna) is the visible, funnel-shaped outer part of the ear that collects sound waves and directs them along the external auditory canal to the eardrum. The auditory ossicles (B), the malleus, incus and stapes, transmit and amplify vibrations in the middle ear. The Eustachian tube (C) equalises air pressure between the middle ear and the throat. The tympanic membrane (D) vibrates when sound waves reach it.

questions.text: A function of the eye pupil is to:

options.A: Transmit impulses from the eye to the brain
options.B: Control the shape of the lens
options.C: Allow light to enter the eye

questions.explanation: Allow light to enter the eye (C) is correct because the pupil is the opening in the centre of the iris; the iris muscles make it smaller in bright light and larger in dim light, controlling how much light reaches the retina. Transmitting impulses from the eye to the brain (A) is the function of the optic nerve. The shape of the lens (B) is controlled by the ciliary muscles. Protecting the eyeball from dust (D) is done by the eyelids, eyelashes and tears.
